IDEAL Tasks — the complete guide

Everything the app does, in one place: every view, every role's permissions, every automated email, and every feature added since launch. Screenshots throughout are from the live app. Use the search box or the menu on the left to jump to any topic.

{{ICON:home}} What is IDEAL Tasks?

A shared task manager built for IDEAL for Digital Transformation — projects, tasks, deadlines, and who's doing what, all in one place, with email reminders so nothing falls through the cracks.

Every task belongs to a project, has one or more assignees (team members or outside contacts), a priority, a status, and dates. From there you can attach files, leave comments, check off subtasks, tag it, duplicate it, or set it to repeat automatically.

Board / List / Timeline views Role-based visibility Email reminders Weekly summary File attachments Installable mobile app

{{ICON:log-in}} Logging in

Accounts are created by a Super Admin from Team Management — there's no public sign-up.

The first time you log in, you'll be asked to set your own password (a temporary one is generated for you when your account is created). If your account is ever deactivated, you'll see a message here instead of the app.

{{ICON:shield}} Roles & what each one can see

Every view in the app — Board, List, Timeline, Reports, Attention, and the weekly email — follows the exact same visibility rule, so what you see is always consistent no matter which screen you're on.

RoleSeesCan manage
Super AdminEvery task, in every projectEverything — team, projects, all tasks, audit log
Project Admin (a grant, not a role)All tasks in the projects they administer, plus their own assigned tasks elsewhereFull edit/delete on tasks within their administered project(s)
MemberOnly tasks assigned to themStatus & progress only, on their own tasks
Project Admin is a grant, not a global role. A Super Admin hands out project-admin rights per project from Manage Team (the folder icon next to a member's name). Someone can be a Project Admin on "Apex Pharmaceutical" and a plain Member everywhere else.
Only a Super Admin can create new projects or add new team members. Everyone else works within what's already been set up for them.

{{ICON:layout}} Board, List & Timeline views

Three ways to look at the same tasks — pick whichever fits what you're doing.

Board

The default view — tasks grouped into four columns: To Do, In Progress, Review, Done. Use the arrows on a card to move it forward or back a stage.

List

A flat, sortable table — better when you want to scan everything at once or sort by a specific column.

Timeline

A Gantt-style calendar strip showing each task's span from start date to due date, so you can spot overlaps and clashes at a glance.

All three share the same toolbar: search, filter by assignee/priority/project, and sort. Every dropdown list (people, projects) is alphabetized.

{{ICON:filter}} Search, filters & saved filters

Narrow down what you're looking at, and keep your favorite combination one click away.

  • Search matches task title and code.
  • Filters: Assignee, Priority, Project — combine as many as you like.
  • Sort: Due Date, Priority, Assignee, or Newest first.
  • Save filter stores your current search + filter + sort combination (by name) so you can jump back to it later — it's saved per person, in your browser.

{{ICON:plus-circle}} Creating & editing a task

Click New Task, or the pencil on any existing task, to open the task form.

Required fields when creating a task

  • Code — a short unique identifier (see "Project codes" below for how this is suggested automatically).
  • Title
  • Project
  • At least one assignee
  • Due Date — always required.
  • Start Date — required unless the task is a Milestone, in which case only one date (Due Date) applies, since a milestone is a single-day marker rather than a date range.
Editing an existing task never blocks you on these rules — they only apply at creation, so older tasks that predate a rule are never locked out of being edited.

Project codes & task numbering

Each project has a short code (e.g. APEX), set once when the project is created. When you pick a project on a new task, the Code field is pre-filled with a suggestion like APEX-0004 — but it's just a suggestion. You can change it to anything; the app won't stop you. This keeps codes tidy by default without forcing rigid numbering on every project.

Duplicating a task

The copy icon on any task creates a fresh copy — same title, assignees, tags, priority and dates, but a new code, status reset to To Do, and progress reset to 0%. From the task form you can also duplicate straight into a different project.

{{ICON:list-checks}} Checklist, attachments, tags & comments

Scroll down inside any task to find its checklist, files, and activity — all in the same place.

Checklist

Lightweight subtasks — check them off as you go. They don't have their own assignee or due date; they're just steps within the task.

Attachments

Attach any file up to 25MB. Files are stored securely and every download link is temporary (expires after a few minutes) — nothing is ever publicly accessible.

Tags

Free-form labels — type a word and press Enter. Use them however makes sense to your team (e.g. onboarding, urgent, client-facing).

Comments & Activity

A running log for the task — your own comments alongside automatic entries for every change (status moves, reassignment, date changes). Nothing is ever deleted from this log.

Recurring tasks

Set a task to repeat Daily, Weekly, or Monthly. The moment it's marked Done, the next occurrence is created automatically with the same details and a due date one interval later — until an optional end date is reached.

Dependencies

Mark a task as depending on another — a purely informational link for now (it doesn't block status changes), useful for seeing what's blocking what.

{{ICON:check-square}} Selecting multiple tasks at once

Click the checkbox icon in the top toolbar to enter select mode, tick the tasks you want, then act on all of them together.

Anyone can bulk-change the status of their own assigned tasks this way. Bulk-changing assignees or moving tasks to another project still requires the same admin rights as editing a single task normally would.

{{ICON:bar-chart}} Reports

A live snapshot, scoped to whatever you're allowed to see.

{{ICON:alert-triangle}} Needs Attention

Everything that's overdue, plus anything high-priority due within 3 days — the two lists most worth checking first thing.

{{ICON:bell}} The notification bell

In-app alerts for anything relevant to you — a new assignment, or a comment on a task you're on.

{{ICON:mail}} Automated emails

Four kinds of email go out automatically — no one has to remember to send them.

EmailWhenSent to
New assignmentThe moment you're added to a taskNewly assigned people only
Due tomorrowOnce, the day before it's dueThe task's assignees
OverdueEvery day it stays overdueAssignees + the project's admins + all Super Admins
Weekly summaryEvery Sunday, 8am Cairo timeEveryone — scoped to what they can see (see below)

What's in the weekly summary

  • Super Admin: the full picture — everything completed, overdue, and due in the next 7 days, across the whole company.
  • Project Admin: the same three sections, scoped to the project(s) they administer, plus their own personal assignments elsewhere.
  • Everyone else: just their own assigned tasks.

{{ICON:users}} Managing the team

Super Admin only. Click the people icon in the top bar.

  • Toggle Inactive instead of deleting — it's reversible, and their past tasks stay exactly as they were.
  • The shield marks Super Admins.
  • The folder icon grants a member admin rights on specific projects.
  • The trash icon permanently deletes the account — a step you can't undo, so Inactive is almost always the better choice.

{{ICON:folder}} Managing projects

Super Admin only. Click the folder/briefcase icon in the top bar.

Deleting a project moves it to Trash rather than removing it outright — its tasks are kept as-is and everything can be restored together.

{{ICON:user-plus}} Managing contacts

Contacts are external people — no login, no account — that you can still assign tasks to.

{{ICON:scroll}} Audit log

Super Admin only — a running history of logins, team changes, and project changes across the whole system. Per-task activity lives on each task instead (see Comments & Activity above); this log is for everything else.

{{ICON:trash}} Trash & restore

Deleted tasks and projects land here first, not gone for good.

{{ICON:file-spreadsheet}} Importing & exporting Excel

Bring in a batch of tasks from a spreadsheet, or pull everything out into one.

  • Download template gives you a blank spreadsheet with the right columns already in place.
  • Import from Excel previews what will be created before committing anything — new projects mentioned in the sheet are created automatically, with a derived project code.
  • Export to Excel pulls everything currently visible to you (respecting your role's normal visibility) into a spreadsheet, mirroring the import template's columns.
Task codes on imported rows are always generated fresh by the app's own numbering system, rather than trusting whatever code was written in the spreadsheet — keeping the same "automatic system" used everywhere else.

{{ICON:smartphone}} Installing IDEAL Tasks on your phone

IDEAL Tasks is a Progressive Web App — you can install it like a native app, no app store required.

On Android (Chrome)

  1. Open the site in Chrome.
  2. Tap the ⋮ menu → Install app (or Add to Home screen).
  3. Confirm — it now opens full-screen from your home screen, with its own icon.

On iPhone (Safari)

  1. Open the site in Safari.
  2. Tap the Share icon → Add to Home Screen.
  3. Confirm — same result: a full-screen app icon on your home screen.
The installed app still talks to the same server — it's a shortcut and an offline-friendly shell, not a separate copy of your data.

{{ICON:help-circle}} Frequently asked questions

I deleted a task by mistake — is it gone?
No — open Trash from the top toolbar. Deleted tasks and projects sit there for 30 days before they're removed for good, and can be restored any time before that.
Why can't I edit a task's title or dates, only its status?
You're not a Super Admin or a Project Admin on that particular project. Anyone assigned to a task can move its status and update progress; changing everything else (title, dates, assignees, project) needs admin rights on that project.
Can I move a task to a different project myself?
Only if you're a Super Admin, or a Project Admin on both the task's current project and the one you're moving it to.
Does changing a task's due date resend the "due tomorrow" email?
Yes — moving the due date resets that reminder, so it will fire again once the new date is one day away.
What happens to a recurring task's history when the next one is created?
The new occurrence is a separate task with a fresh code — it doesn't inherit the old one's comments, checklist, or attachments, only the same title, project, assignees, priority, and a due date one interval later.
Who can see the Audit Log?
Super Admins only. It's a system-wide history (logins, team/project changes) — separate from a task's own Comments & Activity log, which anyone who can open that task can see.
